newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-KLUSENER RIPS THROUGH INDIAN BATTING.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-KLUSENER RIPS THROUGH INDIAN BATTING.

text.p: South African debutant Lance Klusener struck three times to leave India struggling at 59 for four wickets in their second innings on the fourth day of the second test on Saturday.
Chasing a target of 467 runs, the India middle-order once again collasped as Klusener bowled an inspiring spell, claiming three wickets in his 13 overs.
Klusener dismissed opener Nayan Mongia and Saurav Ganguly in a space of four deliveries. V.V.S. Laxman, who was sent ahead of Mohammad Azharuddin was also bowled by Klusener for one.
India started slowly and their three top-order batsman left in quick sucession with only 27 runs on board.
Skipper Sachin Tendulkar was out to a catch at short-leg by Gary Kirsten off spinner Pat Symcox.
Rahul Dravid, on 18, and Mohammad Azharuddin, on 25, prevented further damage.
Azharuddin hit four boundaries in his unbeaten 25 off 24 balls. Dravid stayed on the wicket for nearly 160 minutes, facing 105 balls and scoring only 18 runs.
India still need 408 runs to win, with only six wickets intact.
Nearly 75,000 people thronged the Eden Gardens on Saturday to see the match.
South Africa declared their second innings, just before tea on Saturday, at 367, setting a target of 467 runs for India.
Resuming from an overnight score of 160 for one, South Africa added 207 runs before declaring their innings, helped by two brilliant centuries from Kirsten and Darryl Cullinan.
The pair added 212 before Kirsten was run out for 133 as he tried to steal a quick single. He batted for 315 minutes for his third test century and hit 18 fours.
Cullinan was on 153 not out at the declaration.
